cohort: The study included 543 women who had a copper intrauterine device inserted immediately after delivery at a Brazilian teaching hospital and returned for follow-up.
finding: The overall IUD expulsion rate was 14.7%, with maternal age under 35 years and vaginal delivery identified as significant independent risk factors for expulsion.
mod_finding: IUD expulsion rates were significantly higher after vaginal delivery (22.8%) compared to cesarean section (5.2%), with vaginal delivery being an independent risk factor for expulsion (aOR 5.78).
